note: The scouting ledger: what is known about the register behind each place, so a scout starts from the queue's top and not from whatever is interesting. Written 2026-08-16 after a round drifted into Estonia and Lithuania (#65 and #22) while Toronto, Montreal and Sydney (#8, #10, #14) sat untouched, because the scouting order was coming from the data instead of from the queue. Read by scripts/scout_next.py. Detail and proving sentences live in OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md; this file is the index, one line each.

status_values.imported: a register file exists in data/registers/
status_values.blocked: found, and unusable for a stated reason (licence, non-commercial, withheld locations). Do not re-scout without a new angle.
status_values.stalled: found, reachable, and something specific is in the way. The note says what to try next.
status_values.empty: scouted properly and there is no semantically filtered register. Cheap sources other than a register are the route here.
status_values.unscouted: never actually checked. Being named in a previous pass's 'not reached' list counts as unscouted.

places.note: SCOUTED 2026-08-30 (session), on scout_next.py --target naming Malaga (#14) as no supply/no verdict. Andalusia's REDIAM register (data/registers/andalucia-rediam.json, 749 entries, already imported for the whole region) does hold Malaga-province rows, but they do not help Malaga the CITY: the 20 entries within 30 km are individual rural specimens on farmsteads (cortijos, olive groves, cerros) 8 to 28 km out, none within walking distance of another, none near the city centre or its published cluster (mlg_001-009), and several sit on named private farms with no stated public access, which is a hard rule 10 question the register itself does not answer. This is not a walkable cluster by any reading of the clustering doctrine and none of the 20 is worth a standalone day-trip entry on its own merits (mostly plain olives and carobs judged only by size, no exceptional story). Do not re-query REDIAM for Malaga city supply; it is a dead end there specifically, though the register remains valid for other Andalusian cities. No cheaper route found this pass; a from-zero deepening of Malaga (it is not on Hidde's 2026-08-19 from-zero list) would need Hidde to name it.

SCOUTED 2026-08-21 (night run). Missouri Department of Conservation runs a genuine statewide Champion Trees register (gisblue.mdc.mo.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Land_Cover/Champion_Trees/MapServer/0) with Species, Circumference, Height, Spread, County and a Public_Access YES/NO field, which would otherwise be exactly the kind of semantic, access-aware register this project wants. But it deliberately withholds coordinates: every query, with or without returnGeometry=true, returns an empty geometry object for every record, statewide, not just for private ones (confirmed on unfiltered records too). Hard rule 10 treats a source's own withholding as absolute. Queried Jackson/Clay/Platte/Cass counties (the Missouri side of KC metro): only 1 of the region's champion trees is flagged Public_Access=YES (a Cotinus obovatus at the Vaile Mansion, Independence) and even that one has no coordinates. Do not re-query this service; it is a dead end for locations regardless of filter. A second lead, KC Metro Champion Trees (bridgingthegap.org/kc-metro-champion-trees/, run by Heartland Tree Alliance, covering Jackson/Clay/Platte/Wyandotte/Johnson/NW Cass counties), returns 403 to both curl (with a browser user agent) and WebFetch and was not reached; a session with real browser access should try it before falling back to from-zero research. Kansas's own 'Champion Trees of Kansas' ArcGIS Experience (experience.arcgis.com/experience/2ee620c8178841d5a0084a9a450fe1cc) is unchecked.

SCOUTED 2026-08-21 (night run). No semantically filtered heritage/protected-tree register found. Iceland's nature protection law (log um natturuvernd) lets a single tree be designated a 'natturumyndun' but no searchable list of which trees hold that status turned up. Land og skogur (the merged Skograektin/Landgraedsla, formerly the forestry service) runs an annual 'Tre arsins' (Tree of the Year) honour since 1989, one tree per year nationwide, which is a lead list not a register: no coordinates or dataset, just a name per year on their site. monumentaltrees.com carries an Iceland height-records page (fact-verification only, hard rule 1 forbids reuse). No open-data portal, ArcGIS layer or municipal catalogue found for Reykjavik specifically. Route forward is from-zero web research on Reykjavik's own parks (Hljomskalagardur, Laugardalur, the botanical garden) plus the Tre arsins list as a lead, not a register import.

SCOUTED 2026-08-16. The city's own open data has only the street-tree inventory, which the semantic filter forbids. The real source is the Ontario Heritage Tree Program (Forests Canada / Ontario Urban Forest Council), an ArcGIS FeatureServer behind their StoryMap: 112 trees province-wide with species, an age estimate and a Public/Private flag, 38 within 30 km of Toronto. Its ArcGIS item carries an empty licenseInfo, so it is saved as data/leads/toronto.json (27 public leads, 11 excluded as private land) rather than imported. Next: licence ask to Forests Canada in the next outreach batch.

SCOUTED 2026-08-16. Montreal has a real curated register and it is not on the open-data portal: montroyal.montreal.ca/inventaires, the City's own Site officiel du Mont-Royal, carries 63 individual arbre-remarquable pages, each with per-tree coordinates, the property owner, a planting period, species notes and a written statement of dendrological and cultural interest. Quality is comparable to Sydney's. BLOCKED: montroyal.montreal.ca/credits states '(c) Tous droits reserves, Ville de Montreal', with no reuse terms anywhere on the site. Deliberately NOT scraped, unlike Toronto: Toronto's was an open API with no stated licence, this is website content with an explicit all-rights-reserved notice, and copying the compilation is not the same act as querying an open endpoint. donnees.montreal.ca carries only the full public-tree inventory, which the semantic filter forbids. Next: licence ask to the Bureau du Mont-Royal.

SOLVED the endpoint 2026-08-16 and blocked on licence. City of Sydney Register of Significant Trees, 2,504 entries, ArcGIS FeatureServer services1.arcgis.com/cNVyNtjGVZybOQWZ/ArcGIS/rest/services/Register_of_Significant_Trees_view/FeatureServer/0, open and queryable. It is the richest register found anywhere: species, common name, height, spread, year_of_planting, statement_of_significance, address, owner, and two fields the corpus says registers never have, condition (coded, including Dead) and accessibilility (Public access / Visible from street / No public access). BUT the AGOL item carries an empty licenseInfo, the dataset is not on the CC BY 4.0 data hub, and cityofsydney.nsw.gov.au's own terms say content must not be reproduced without written authorisation. Not imported, and the refusal is now explicit rather than merely absent: the register sweep found the City's own sibling layers 'RST Existing view' and 'RST Future nomination view', both carrying licenseInfo 'For public viewing only inside of City of Sydney Significant Tree Register. Not for individual re-use.' So this is a stated no, not an oversight, and the licence ask sent 2026-08-16 is the only route. Next: a licence request to the City, which is Hidde's to send.

SCOUTED 2026-08-16. The city's own open data has only 'Trees in the City', a public-tree inventory the semantic filter forbids. The real source is the National Trust of Western Australia's Significant Tree Register, published as a PDF (nationaltrustwa.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/National-Trust-Significant-Tree-Register-November-2024.pdf, readable, 64 entries parsed): code, common name, a count, and a street address. 24 entries are Perth metro, including the Fremantle Proclamation Tree. Several are avenues or groups (one of 73, one of 38) that fail the collectible-point test. NO coordinates, so every entry needs geocoding, and NO licence is stated; the National Trust WA is a charity, so this is a permission ask like the others. inHerit, the state heritage database, also carries 'Significant Trees' records but is explicitly All Rights Reserved and its entries are vague groupings including back-yard trees.

Significant Tree is a state Development Act designation administered per council (Adelaide, Burnside, Prospect, Unley), so it is several lists rather than one fetch. Next: check whether SA's planning portal publishes a consolidated overlay.

FOUND 2026-08-23 (night run), superseding the 2026-08-13 'named but not reached' entry. City of Vancouver Heritage Register, category 'LANDSCAPE RESOURCES Trees' (opendata.vancouver.ca, dataset heritage-sites): 51 tree entries, 25 with a real street address and named species (Giant Sequoia, Northern Red Oak, English Oak, Tulip Tree, Fernleaf Beech, Garry Oak, Copper Beech, Caucasian Wing-Nut and more), 26 are streetscape rows with no address (blocked, not single collectible points). NO COORDINATES in the source, only street address (often a number range), so this is not import-ready as a register: saved as data/leads/vancouver.json instead. Next step for a build/verify pass: geocode each address, then run the normal two-source verify pass.

SOLVED 2026-08-16, scripts/jp_kyoju.py. Three things had to be found and none is guessable: pagination is _command=changepage with a ZERO-BASED page number (js/pager.js), the CSRF token ROTATES on every response so each request must carry the previous page's token, and place_filter=3 is a fake radius search that returns the national total of 76,368 whatever marker you give it. All three fail silently with HTTP 200 and a re-rendered empty form, so a crawler that misses any of them reads one page of a thousand-record prefecture and reports success. Only place_filter=1 with prefecture_code filters. The licence caveat is solved by a FIELD rather than judgement: every row carries ユーザ, and the ministry's own 1988/2000 survey records read 'Admin', so citizen submissions (whose copyright stays with the poster, outside PDL 1.0) are excluded mechanically. CORRECTION to the 2026-08-04 entry, which said the database gives 'girth, height, species, and location': there are NO COORDINATES. Location is prefecture, municipality and an address line, and the schema carries a position-disclosure field with a reason-for-withholding beside it, which is hard rule 10 written into the source. So it is a lead source, not a map layer, and pinning is a separate job. Hiroshima done: data/leads/hiroshima.json, 102 ministry records, with girth, species and a vitality field (67 good, 24 partly dead, 4 near death). Remaining prefectures are one command each: 1 Hokkaido/Sapporo, 23 Aichi/Nagoya, 28 Hyogo/Kobe, 14 Kanagawa/Kamakura.
Portugal ICNF (arvoredo de interesse publico) is imported nationally and covers Sintra. Not a scouting gap, a ledger gap: the tool read it as unscouted because nobody had written the line.
Andalucia REDIAM is imported and covers Cadiz. Ledger gap rather than a scouting gap. Cadiz ships 5 trees and is a finished compact city per CLAUDE.md, so the gap-to-10 is not a target.

SCOUTED 2026-08-17, and the answer is a negative worth keeping. The Regione Siciliana DOES publish its own Elenco degli Alberi Monumentali di Sicilia (updated 17.07.2026, on regione.sicilia.it), covering the whole island including Catania and Messina, so it looks at first like the regional unlock that Campania and Lazio turned out to be. It is not. It is the SAME underlying dataset as the national MASAF register: same sheet ids, same decree D.M. n. 5450 del 19/12/2017, identical girth and height figures, republished with one field added, the criteri di monumentalita saying why each tree was designated, plus a yes/no on proposal for notevole interesse pubblico. NO age field and NO vitality field, which are the two things a page needs most and the two things Campania's per-tree cards and Lazio's xlsx actually provide. It also does NOT count as a second independent source on top of MASAF, because it is the same data. Do not re-scout this: for Sicilian cities, age and vitality still have to come from a garden's own records, a university page or the local press, one tree at a time.

IMPORTED 2026-08-23 (night run), scouted 2026-08-17. Next step for a build/verify pass: claim Tenerife, identify which park the 60-tree cluster actually is, and verify the first 6 to 8 toward the existing 4-tree page's target. The Cabildo's separate island-wide 12-tree JS portal remains unscouted for licence, as before.

SCOUTED 2026-08-17 (island scout, Atlantic group). Authority: Cabildo de Gran Canaria, Catalogo Insular de Arboles Singulares (Decreto 15 November 2021), plus a separate municipal catalogue for the capital: Ayuntamiento de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. URL: https://custodiadelterritorio.grancanaria.com/en/arboles-singulares (insular, per-tree 'ficha' pages on a Liferay CMS); https://lpgcsostenible.laspalmasgc.es/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Catalogo_arboles_LPGC.pdf (municipal, 326 specimens across 181 fichas). Licence: NOT PROVEN for either source. The insular custodiadelterritorio.grancanaria.com page fetched clean (HTTP 200, 320KB) but is a per-tree CMS page with no licence statement found in the fetched HTML head or footer. The municipal PDF sits on lpgcsostenible.laspalmasgc.es, whose /aviso-legal returned a 301 redirect this pass did not follow (time-boxed); no licence sentence quotable yet from either. Until one is fetched and quoted, both stay ungated for import despite good data.. Fields: Insular catalogue (per news coverage, not yet fetched from a per-tree ficha this pass): age (explicitly, up to 400 years for the oldest, e.g. the acebuche of Llano Parra and the sabina of Tirma), a visitability/access flag (11 of the insular 77-85 are recorded as not accessible to visitors, which is exactly the field hard rule 10 needs), species, dimensions. Municipal PDF: not opened this pass, format and fields unconfirmed beyond '326 specimens, 181 fichas' from press coverage.. Count: Insular: sources disagree, 77 or 85 selected from a field survey of 273 candidates (both figures appear in different press pieces, so treat as approximate until the primary source is read). Municipal (Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, the capital): 326 specimens across 181 fichas, covering the whole city, so likely several within any walkable cluster of the capital.. Genuinely promising: this is the first Canary source in this pass with an AGE field and an explicit access/visitability flag, which is rarer than most mainland Spanish regional registers this project has imported. What is in the way is purely licence proof and structured data extraction, not a designation question. Next steps for whoever picks this up: (1) fetch https://lpgcsostenible.laspalmasgc.es/aviso-legal with -L to follow the redirect and quote its reuse terms, or find a dedicated Cabildo/Ayuntamiento open-data portal (datos.grancanaria.com or similar, searched for but not found this pass); (2) if no open licence exists, the per-tree custodiadelterritorio fichas may still be usable as a verification source under the same rules as monumentaltrees.com, i.e. one browser-viewed page at a time, never bulk. Also worth noting for whoever verifies: the insular catalogue's own legal basis is unsettled (a legal report found the Cabildo lacks competence to enforce the ordinance pending a regional biodiversity law), which affects protection status, not whether the trees themselves are real, old or worth a visit.

SCOUTED 2026-08-20. DataSF's Street Tree List (tkzw-k3nq) carries a qLegalStatus field, and filtering it to 'Landmark tree' is a semantic filter rather than the forbidden bulk inventory: 244 trees individually designated by city ordinance. LICENCE IS CLEAN, PDDL 1.0, public domain, which CLAUDE.md names as acceptable. 187 are maintained by DPW or Rec/Park, so the visitor stands on the pavement. THE CATCH, and it is most of the story: 167 of those 187 are Canary Island Date Palms on Dolores Street, one designated avenue planting, which is the La Rambla case and is at most ONE entry rather than 167. What is left is a stand of 12 blue gums at 1661 Octavia and a handful of singletons, several of them modest ornamentals. So San Francisco's real trees (the Presidio cypresses, Golden Gate Park, the Moon Tree) need from-zero research; the landmark register alone does not open the city.

SCOUTED 2026-08-20, not yet mined. The Louisiana Garden Club Federation has registered live oaks since 1934 and the roll now passes 10,000 trees across 14 states, published as PDFs on lgcfinc.org with registration number, tree name, location, parish, girth and sponsor. Junior League is 8 to 16 feet of girth, Centenarian is over 16. NEW ORLEANS CITY PARK ALONE HOLDS 249 REGISTERED TREES, which is a dense walkable cluster in a public park in a city we do not cover. No coordinates in the roll, so pins need separate work, and girths are in feet. It is a garden club rather than a government body, so treat it as a lead and verification source like Nevada and Texas, never an import. Serves New Orleans (#160), Savannah (#207), Charleston, Baton Rouge and Mobile.

SCOUTED 2026-08-20 and it is not the shortcut it looks like. The programme moved from American Forests to the University of Tennessee in 2023 (nationalchampiontree.org). No API found; the WordPress REST endpoint carries no tree post type and the register is published as PDFs. More to the point, champion trees are champions by species points and mostly stand in remote forests and on ranches: the Texas equivalent, which we did sweep, held only 13 to 28 trees within 40 km of each big city, most of them on private land. A national champion register is not a route to urban trees.

SWEPT 2026-08-20 across both indexes that matter. Socrata's federated catalogue (api.us.socrata.com) returns exactly one US heritage/landmark tree dataset, Norfolk's Significant Trees. ArcGIS Hub returns a long tail of small municipalities and student projects (Mountain View has nine near-duplicate layers from San Jose State) plus Fort Worth. No big-audience US city publishes one this way. Portland is the exception and is already imported. Conclusion: there is no index shortcut for US cities; the route is per city, and the Austin result says a STORY register beats a measurement register when one exists.

SOLVED 2026-08-20 and it is the best per-tree source on this site. The arboretum publishes an accession-level ArcGIS feature service at services1.arcgis.com/qN3V93cYGMKQCOxL/arcgis/rest/services/Sci_Name_and_Acc_Num/FeatureServer/0 carrying LATITUDE/LONGITUDE to eight decimals, ACC_NUM, DBH, HEIGHT, CIRCUMFERENCE with MEASURE_DT, CONDITION, CHECK_DT, GARDEN_LOCATION and an IS_DEAD flag, which no tree register anywhere else has. It moved two Boston pins on the day it was found, by 315 and 255 metres, and needed no inference because our own stories already named the accessions. TWO TRAPS. PLANT_DT is a database date, not a planting date: the 1948 dawn redwood reads 2003, and the accession number is the age signal (3-48 and 524-48 are 1948 accessions). And an accession can carry several plants (*A, *B, *C) hundreds of metres apart, so matching on accession alone can still leave two candidates; where nothing separates them the pin stays approximate. Find it via arcgis.com/sharing/rest/search?q=Arnold+Arboretum; the arboretum's own website returns 403 to plain curl.

places.note: SCOUTED 2026-08-20 while trying to sharpen New York's twelve approximate pins, six of them in Central Park. NYC OpenData's Forestry Tree Points (hn5i-inap) has species, dbh, condition and a live update date, but it is a STREET tree layer: a 400 m query around the Central Park West pin returned 300 sidewalk trees (London plane, pin oak, Callery pear) and nothing from the park interior, which the Central Park Conservancy manages separately. The Conservancy's own tree map has no reachable endpoint (maps.centralparknyc.org does not resolve, /tree-map is a 404). So New York's pins need per-tree work, not a data source, and nobody should re-run this sweep.

SCOUTED 2026-08-23 (night run), Asheville #56, no ledger entry until now. The N.C. Forest Service Champion Tree List (ncagr.gov/divisions/nc-forest-service/nc-champion-tree-list, xlsx download, 379 rows, last updated January 2026) is a real statewide semantic register with species, circumference/height/spread, county and an Owner Authorized Public Access and Viewing Yes/No field, including a Buncombe County entry (Nordmann fir, public access Yes). BLOCKED outright, same as Missouri's Champion Trees: the file's own cover sheet states plainly that specific location information for each tree is not listed due to landowner privacy concerns. No address, no coordinates, not even a place name beyond county. Hard rule 10 treats a source's own withholding as absolute; there is no coordinate to approximate from and no lead to extract, only a species-and-county fact that could at most corroborate a tree found some other way. Do not re-download this file expecting different fields; it is a dead end for locations by explicit design, not an oversight. Next step for Asheville, if pursued: from-zero web research (parks department, Botanical Gardens at Asheville, Biltmore Estate's own published trees) rather than any register.

SCOUTED 2026-08-23 (Turku #67, no supply, no verdict). Finland has a real national designation, "luonnonmuistomerkki" (natural monument) under the Nature Conservation Act, individual trees/groups/boulders protected by municipality or Metsahallitus decision, exactly the semantic-filter shape wanted. Split across three sources, none import-ready for Turku today. (1) The national dataset that would cover Turku, Metsahallitus/SYKE "Luonnonmuistomerkit" (ckan.ymparisto.fi/dataset/luonnonmuistomerkit, nationwide ZIP/shapefile plus WMS): licence NOT proven, CKAN's own license_id/license_title are null and the page only says "no limitations" on access, not a named licence; its WFS endpoint returned "Service WFS is disabled" when queried; Turku's own region (Varsinais-Suomi) is outside the five regions the source itself calls field-verified. (2) Turku's own city WFS (turku.asiointi.fi/TeklaOGCWeb/WFS.ashx, layer kanta:SuojeltavaKohde) DOES carry these exact points (tyyppi=luonnonmuistomerkki, confirmed live), but with no species/name/age/description field at all, only geometry and a digitisation date; the surrounding "Turun kaupungin paikkatietoja" dataset is stated CC BY 4.0 but that listing never names this layer specifically, so the licence match is a strong inference, not a verbatim proving sentence for this exact layer. (3) Helsinki (a different city, not Turku) has a fully confirmed, fully populated equivalent: avoindata:LTJ_avoin_rauhoitettu_luonnonmuistomerkit at kartta.hel.fi, CC BY 4.0 confirmed both on Helsinki's general open geographic data page and on the dataset's own avoindata.suomi.fi listing, 31 live GeoJSON features with name, description (girth/height in free text) and coordinates. Import-ready for Helsinki, not for Turku. Full detail in OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md.

SCOUTED 2026-08-31 (session, with a browser). The California Registry of Big Trees, californiabigtrees.calpoly.edu, run by Cal Poly's Urban Forest Ecosystems Institute. The previous US pass recorded this as a React app whose data API could not be resolved; it is resolved now. The bundle calls `Wl.get('/bigtrees/getAllBt')` against a base constant `zl` of https://www.selectree.calpoly.edu/api, so the whole registry is one fetch: https://www.selectree.calpoly.edu/api/bigtrees/getAllBt returns 266 rows of JSON, no key, no login. SHAPE: excellent. Per tree it carries latitude and longitude at tree level, accepted scientific and common name, family, height, crown width, circumference, date_measured, county, nominator and measurer names, a photo path, and flags for state_champion, national_champion, co_champion, hidden and DEAD. A dead flag is the field almost no register has. 229 of the 266 are live, unhidden and located. It is a champion-tree register (biggest known specimen per species, by nomination), so it passes the semantic filter cleanly: it is a curated designation, not a municipal inventory, which is what disqualified Seattle, San Francisco, Savannah and San Diego. COUNTY SPREAD relevant to our queue: Los Angeles 54, Santa Barbara 24, Sacramento 14, Santa Clara 12, Orange 11, San Diego 8. Sacramento (#134) and San Diego (#138) are ranked cities standing at zero. WHY STALLED, and it is the only thing missing: NO DATA LICENCE IS STATED ANYWHERE. The site carries a liability disclaimer ('No warranties or guarantees as to the accuracy of the data...'), which is not a licence, and neither californiabigtrees.calpoly.edu, selectree.calpoly.edu nor ufei.calpoly.edu publishes terms of use for the data. The only licences on those pages belong to their WordPress theme and their CSS library. No licence stated is a stall and not a yes. THE PATH IS ONE EMAIL. The site publishes its own contact, mritter@calpoly.edu, for questions. A draft asking permission is at drafts/OUTREACH.md; sending it is Hidde's, per hard rule 4. UNITS WARNING for whoever imports it after permission: this is a US champion-tree register, so height is almost certainly FEET, circumference INCHES and crown width FEET, and none of it is labelled. Prove the units against the physical world before trusting a number, the way the Hawaii import had to.
